themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints spiked to 26 THIS WEEK, a 447% surge above the 4.8-complaint weekly average tracked over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a rapid deterioration in street-level homelessness on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 26 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Concurrent 140% spike in panhandling complaints (6 THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 avg) suggests broader street-level disorder surge
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Where are encampments concentrated? Interview residents, NYPD, and NYC Homeless Services for causes of sudden spike
Policy angle: How is the city's encampment response unit deployed on UES? Are there adequate shelter beds or social services capacity?

themes_detail.label: Street Light Outages Widespread
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints exploded to 31 three weeks ago, a 368% spike above the 6.6-complaint weekly average, with a z-score of 8.13—one of the district's most statistically anomalous issues, indicating possible systemic infrastructure failure.
evidence: 31 street light complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
368% spike with z-score of 8.13 (highest statistical severity in dataset)
Aligns with community board's repeated budget requests for street infrastructure repairs
reporting_angles: Con Ed accountability: Which blocks or corridors are darkest? Has Con Ed responded to the spike or is there a known outage?
Safety angle: Do residents report increased crime, accidents, or quality-of-life concerns linked to unlit streets?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped to 9 two weeks ago, a 140% spike above the 3.8-complaint weekly average, suggesting either new dumping hotspots or increased resident reporting of a sanitation enforcement gap.
evidence: 9 illegal dumping complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Broader sanitation concerns: unsanitary condition complaints remain at 359 total over 90 days, indicating persistent neighborhood cleanliness issues
reporting_angles: Ground map: Where are dumping hotspots clustered? Are they near construction sites, parking lots, or residential areas?
Enforcement gap: Is DSNY response time adequate? Are there repeat offenders or organized dumping operations?

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Reports Surge
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 5 three weeks ago, a 700% surge above the 0.6-complaint weekly average with z-score 6.29, likely driven by building renovation activity—131 alteration filings and 22 demolitions in prior 90 days—raising health and disclosure concerns.
evidence: 5 asbestos complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
700% spike with z-score of 6.29 (severe statistical anomaly)
1766 DOB building permits filed over 90 days (1579 alterations, 22 demolitions) creates high-risk exposure window for asbestos disturbance
reporting_angles: Health investigation: Are residents near renovation sites reporting respiratory symptoms? Has DOB cited contractors for improper asbestos handling?
Regulatory angle: How many of the 1579 alteration permits include asbestos surveys? Are developers complying with disclosure requirements?

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints doubled to 8 last week, a 392% spike above the 1.6-complaint weekly average, though the category is ambiguous; investigation is needed to clarify if this reflects traffic enforcement, vendor crackdowns, or other city operations.
evidence: 8 real-time enforcement complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Category definition unclear in 311 data—requires source verification to determine if related to traffic, street vendors, or other enforcement actions
reporting_angles: Clarification call: Contact 311 and DOE/NYPD to define 'real-time enforcement' complaints and identify the source of the spike
Impact check: Are residents reporting more traffic stops, vendor tickets, or summonses in the past week?
